fichas.title: Conservatories
fichas.summary: Conservatories project from living rooms and have large glazed areas. Historically, they were heated by sunlight and naturally ventilated, serving as climatic buffer zones and protecting plants during the cold part of the year. They are now commonly used as extensions of living space, especially in spring and autumn. Additional heating and automatic ventilation can support subtropical plants; conservatories incorporated into the heated building volume require an appropriately designed outer envelope. Illustrated forms include projecting, corner, external-corner, recessed, and transverse-projecting conservatories, as well as conservatories spanning an entire building width.
uses: Protect plants in the cold season
Accommodate subtropical plants when equipped with additional heating and automatic ventilation
